newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese police seize big cocaine haul.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese police seize big cocaine haul.

text.p: Lebanese police have seized most of a shipment of 130 kg (286 pounds) of pure cocaine worth some $13 million smuggled into Lebanon through Beirut port, police officials said on Tuesday.
They said 14 people have been arrested in various Lebanese areas in connection with the shipment, which came from Venezuela. The drugs had been packed in a container labelled construction material.
"Most of the cocaine has been seized in several areas," one official, who declined to be named, told Reuters. He did not say when the drugs were smuggled into Lebanon.
The drugs are estimated of have a wholesale value of about $13 million in Lebanon, officials added.

Lebanese authorities began a campaign against the drugs trade in Lebanon in 1992 and announced earlier this year that cannabis and opium poppy cultivation has been eradicated but some small heroin processing plants remain to be destroyed.

The authorities have also thwarted several attempts to smuggle in drugs from abroad, especially cocaine, including one shipment of more than 500 kg (1,100 pounds) of cocaine from Brazil through Beirut airport in August 1995.
